The city of Strife was long thought to be an impregnable fortress. Many invading armies in the past had tried their hand at scaling her walls, fighting their way through the front gates or sneaking in under the cover of night to lay siege. Phainon thought all of these people must have been very stupid to invade a city full of gladiators who slept with spears under their pillows just waiting for an excuse to use them, but what did he know?

Castrum Kremnos’ palace would never be successfully infiltrated by any foreign invader for the very foundation it was built upon… but what about just one man?

This question haunted him ever since he fell into this particular line of business, which is to say, thievery. It wasn't what he imagined himself doing when he was a boy, but it put food on the table and gave him a rush like no other. What could he say? He was an adrenaline junkie through and through. What the rest of Amphoreus assumed were the dastardly deeds of a clandestine network of highly trained, elite operatives was really just one man who had to aim higher and higher each time to get the same high that came from a job well done.

Thus brought him to the walls of Kremnos’ very pregnable palace on one warm summer's eve with but one goal in mind; To steal the crown jewels of Kremnos.

Thought to be the most beautiful assortment of gemstones in all the land, they adorned the crown prince's head everywhere he went as if to invite the challenge of taking them. Phainon travelled halfway across the continent just to see them for himself.

It was at a parade held in honor of the prince's recent engagement. Phainon watched from the crowd as the dromas pulling the royal family's festive cart slowly strolled down the streets, giving his people enough time to throw petals and streamers and raise their spears to him. In that moment, he felt the stars align as the prince turned to face him the exact moment he passed by, the light hitting that ruby soldered to the center of his diadem in such a way that it appeared to shine brighter than the sun itself. Phainon had to swallow down his own drool, not for the prince's otherworldly beauty or absurd physique, but for the luster of the rubies fixed to his strawberry blond hair and the sapphires adorning his chiseled collarbone.

In that very moment, Phainon decided those jewels would one day be his.

There was just one problem… the prince was to be wed to a foreigner.

Come sunrise, he would be on a carriage bound for Ladon, and those precious stones would slip right through Phainon’s fingers for good. Phainon was a lot of things, but a man who was willing to step foot in that hellhole was not one of them. If he wanted Kremnos’ crown jewels, it would have to be tonight.

Ordinarily, Phainon would spend months on a job like this, getting a lay of the land, figuring out which jilted employees he could exploit for floor plans and guard details and routines, compiling his wealth of knowledge to concoct the perfect crime, slipping in and out completely undetected and leaving behind another of history's greatest unsolved heists in his wake…

This time, it was surprisingly simple. All he had to do was tell the front guard he wanted to challenge the King to a duel for the throne and they let him right through. As it turned out, the fortress which was equipped to weather any storm and repel any foreign invader was quite vulnerable to being broken into by just one guy. He gave the same story to each guard he passed.

“You there! What do you think you're doing in here!?”

“Challenging the King.”

“...Very well. Strife be with you.”

It was so ridiculous that he couldn't really fault anyone for not trying in the past. Kremnoans liked their bloodshed, but they were not so senseless about it that entering the palace was a sure death sentence. As long as you had the right excuse, anything went. One guard even gave him directions when they noticed he was walking the wrong way. He wondered how Kremnos’ adversaries had gone so long without figuring out that their society actively invited anyone brave enough to waltz into the palace and try killing their King in ritualistic combat, but that kind of politicking was a bit above his pay grade. He wouldn't mind divulging his secrets for the right price, though.

The whole palace cleared out ahead of the final day of festivities, a series of gladiatorial events held in the prince's honor, after which he was expected to deliver one final farewell to his people. All that stood between Phainon and his prize was blue skies and sunshine. Did this make the gratification he gleaned from success ultimately feel cheap and unsatisfying, leading to him taking bigger and bigger risks until eventually reaching a point of no return? Who cares. Red wasn't his color, but he bet that crown would look dashing on him.

His trek across the castle was silent, eerie in a way. When halls were designed wide enough to hold as many servants and guards as necessary while preventing traffic jams, it made it hard not to notice when they were completely empty. He scaled one stairway and followed down another, crossing a terrace decorated with trellises of grapes and marigolds before entering a seemingly endless corridor, checking behind each door he passed before coming upon yet another staircase, which seemed to lead up to a secluded tower. The moment he swung the doors open, Phainon knew he had found what he was looking for; The prince's chambers.

A luxurious carpet sprawled across the floor from end to end, each wall decorated with tapestries depicting famed Kremnoan mythos alongside some of the prince's very own feats on the battlefield. Someone was full of themselves. His bed overlooked the eastern mountains through two massive marble pillars leading out to a balcony where he grew his own tomatoes and pomegranates, among other pretty flowering plants. Phainon plucked a few from the vine and popped them into his mouth before heading back inside for what he really came for. The prince left it out just for him.

Neatly set atop a silken pillow on the prince's vanity was none other than the crown jewels. Phainon could've blushed. The diadem was even more beautiful up close, a base made of winding gold alloy shaped of olive branches, shimmering with a freshly polished luster and spliced with beads of small rubies and corals. The largest gemstone was placed right in the center, holding both distinct end pieces together with delicate branches twisting it in place.

The level of craftsmanship required to forge such a piece was almost unfathomable. Kremnoan blacksmiths were hailed as some of the best in the world for a reason. Phainon touched it as though it was made of glass, shivering at the feel of cool metal against his skin before lifting it from the pillow. Light spilling in from the open terrace wrapped around its frame and accentuated all of its finer details even more gloriously.

Finally, just as Phainon was about to place the diadem in his own hair, he heard something.

A rustle, from just beyond the door.

He panicked, stowing the crown beneath his coat and ducking for cover. The open concept of the room worked entirely against him, leaving him with only one viable option short of fleeing out to the balcony. Phainon bolted for the bed, crawling onto his knees and diving beneath the skirt, frantically flattening it back out to conceal his hiding spot before the doors swung open.

Phainon listened in total darkness as a pair of heavy boots stomped across the carpet, holding his breath and praying that whoever had come in wasn't in the mood for a very long nap.

Footsteps carried the mysterious intruder (ironic coming from him, he knew) across the room, kicking out a chair which Phainon knew to be beside the desk before wooden drawers flew open, one sounding as though it had actually come loose from its hinges and crashed to the floor. Whoever this person was, they must’ve been angry about something. Phainon could practically hear the steam billowing from their nostrils with each breath they took. Just his luck that an enraged bull would come charging through!

Pen scratched papyrus, and Phainon flattened onto his stomach to quietly crawl forward just far enough to lift the bed skirt and survey the situation without blowing his cover. To his horror, he was greeted by the sight of a pair of bronze boots turned to face the opposite wall. And not just any boots, either… Those were the prince's boots!

He was back? Already!? His own festival had barely just begun!

The prince faced away from him while harshly scribbling his anger onto the scroll, occasionally stopping to furiously scrub his one sleeve against his face. He abruptly stopped and turned around without warning, forcing Phainon to throw a hand over his mouth and drop the skirt. His heart lurched up to his throat, shallow, ragged breaths superheating the air against his face and turning the thick decorative skirt into a furnace. He was by no means claustrophobic, but he would be a fool not to fear being caught by Kremnos’ savage crown prince. He didn't reckon an oak bedframe could stop a spear from hurtling through the mattress and staking him to the floor.

Finally, Phainon heard footsteps travel across the room again, to where he knew the prince's vanity to be. There, he would find an empty pillow where his crown once was. There was no sound, no sudden movement, no indication at all that he had even acknowledged the missing diadem. The suspense was going to eat Phainon alive!

He dared one last peek, relief flooding his veins once he saw that the prince was still turned around. He watched the prince's back muscles tense sharply before sinking with a heavy exhale. He grabbed his spear off the wall and walked forward, right past the bed and out to the balcony. Phainon kicked forward and followed his path to one of his beloved shrubs, twisting a pomegranate right off the vine before cracking it open with the tip of his spear. Phainon flinched, face scrunching up as he imagined his skull in place of that pomegranate, once the prince caught him lurking beneath the bed. Or maybe some other distinctly round part of his body that he's certain he wouldn't want a spear anywhere near.

Even the way he scooped up pomegranate seeds was violent, digging into the fruit with his bare hands, spraying juices all over his fingers and chomping down like he was tearing through raw flesh with his teeth. Phainon pitied the man who got the crown prince's panties in a twist– on second thought, maybe he should save that pity for himself.

The prince tossed aside his half eaten pomegranate and wiped his face on his bare arm, tucking his spear under his armpit while walking towards the ornate, geometric bannister. There, he got on one knee to silently place his spear flat on the ground before picking himself up and looking out across the mountaintops, in the same direction as his new home to the east.

A heavy silence blanketed the terrace, one broken only by the summertime breeze as it whistled through his foliage and the patterns carved into the rail. The prince turned his head up to it, shoulders raising with a deep, zen breath before lowering again. Then, he…

He climbed up…?

The prince stood on the bannister, overlooking a ledge no less than a hundred meters above the ground. Oh God, he wasn't going to-?

Oh. He was. He was going to jump!

Phainon saw his life flash before his eyes, over a decade of well planned, well executed heisting brought to a screeching halt after one of his grandest exploits yet resulted in the death of a prince. A prince of Kremnos, no less! Oh, they would hang him by his pinkie toes, once they found him. And they would find him. Serves him right for cutting corners and not doing his due diligence!

Sure, he knew his moral compass was a bit skewed, but the one and only rule he would never, ever compromise on was the clause of ‘do no harm.’ Not to the people he stole from, not to accidental witnesses who happened to stumble in at the wrong time, not to the authorities who put a bounty on his head. This was all harmless fun, stealing the equivalent of pennies from people who hoarded wealth like water during a drought and funneling it back to the people who actually needed it… most of the time… Admittedly, he did like to keep a few things for himself, every now and again, but– that wasn't important right now!

Even if he really did love that crown, he didn't want the prince to kill himself over it!

“W-Wait!” Phainon shrieked, banging his head on the bottom of the bedframe as he scrambled out from his cover.

The speed at which the prince turned nearly gave Phainon whiplash, a look of bewilderment across his face as his outspread arms raised defensively to his chest.

“Who in Nikador’s name are you!?” Prince Mydeimos shouted accusatorily from the ledge. “If you're another assassin, you should know that the last five never made it past these walls again. Would you like to see why?”

“No! No! I'm not an assassin, I swear it!” Phainon rubbed the back of his head to soothe the emerging goose egg as he shamefully crawled across the floor, stumbling up to his legs. “I– I am, uh…” Phainon's voice trailed off. His thoughts were all scrambled, both from the suddenness of the interrogation and the collision. He didn't love the idea of telling the prince his real name, just in case he could still find a way out of this monumental screw up, but there was no time to cook up a believable enough lie, either! “I am the second greatest thief in all of Amphoreus! And I think a better question would be ‘what in Nikador’s name are you doing!?’”

Mydeimos looked around, first to his feet, then over the ledge, then back to Phainon. “Is… is it not obvious?” he asked. Did he think Phainon was stupid!?

“I mean- I know what you're doing, but- why!” And oh, Kephale above, why now!? “If the crown really means so much to you, you can have it back. I'd much rather be hung for burglarizing the palace than tortured and skinned alive for shoving the prince to his death!”

The prince looked half offended, a sour sneer across his face. “I don't care about the crown. You can keep it, for all I care. It has brought me nothing but misery. You should leave now before they discover my body.”

Phainon's face scrunched up, sucking in a sharp breath. “That's kinda no good for me, Prince Mydeimos. See, I only came here for this. This right here,” Phainon said, unfurling his coat and revealing the diadem, clinking a golden branch with his nail. “And I'd kind of like to avoid getting nailed for first degree murder, if I can! I mean- you see how this would look for me, right!?”

Mydeimos eyed him up and down with a glare. “...I'm going to jump now.”

“Stop threatening to jump!” Phainon cried. Gods, he was bad at this. In his defense, he was not planning on talking anyone down from any ledges today, and he never had the makings of a mental health professional. “Why don't we just talk about this, yeah?”

Mydeimos scoffed, blowing a piece of air out of his face. “Talk about what?”

Phainon blinked. “Uh… I don't, really… oh! Okay, how about that letter you wrote?” he suggested, frantically grasping at whatever straws sturdy enough to get them both out of this alive. “Let's talk about that.”

The prince's eyelids flattened. Drat, he was losing him again. “What's there to talk about? My father has already made up his mind and so have I. I would rather die with my dignity than become the broodmare for some piggish, fat old monarch across the mountains. Can you leave now? You're very irritating and I'd like to spend my last few minutes in solitude.”

Phainon croaked, half-offended. “Well, we know he isn't marrying you for your personality,” he muttered under his breath.

Mydeimos deadpanned before fanning out his arms and slipping a boot off the ledge. Phainon's heart dropped to his ass, and he halfway collapsed to the floor to beg the prince's forgiveness for his imprudence. Thankfully, just seeing his full-body panic sufficed in bringing the prince back over the balcony.

“I gave you the option to walk away, and you refused it. Good luck escaping with your life when a thousand guards swarm the castle looking for the man who did this. In my father's eyes, even my death could not be my own choice.”

Phainon was running out of options here. It was as if the Fates had already decided the outcome of this encounter, that one or both of them must die, whether it be by choice or pure happenstance. Phainon nearly chewed a hole through his bottom lip. Oh, his poor mother, who would one day soon learn that her son had been ripped to a million pieces by an angry mob after being paraded through the streets of Kremnos as the honorless whelp who ambushed and killed their prince in his own bedroom…

…That's it! If Atropos wanted her blood so badly, then she would have it in spades!

“Fine. You really want to die that bad? Go ahead. Just know that once you do, I'm coming down with you,” Phainon declared, digging his heel into the marble in a display of staunch conviction.

The prince's face paled, painted aghast with his shock. “What? No, you can't-”

“I can and I will! In fact, after you jump, I'm going to crumple up that note you left and write a new one exposing all the gritty, raunchy details of our whirlwind romance!”

“...What!?”

“Oh, didn't you know? We were in love, you and I. So in love, in fact, that you just couldn't live without me! After I snuck in to meet you on our final night together and saw what you'd done, I cast myself into the gorge to join you in death so that we would never have to be apart again!”

Mydeimos stood completely still, frozen all but for the wind blowing through his hair and fluttering the tail of his robe. The resting scowl on his face began to deepen until it was a hideous, disgusted frown. Then, and only then, did Mydeimos finally descend the ledge.

“I think I'd rather just hold off, in that case,” he muttered, picking up his spear and shuffling back towards his room.

He may as well have staked Phainon through the chest. “Okay. Ouch.”

Mydeimos stopped just before one of the massive support columns on the precipice of the balcony before his head swivelled in Phainon's direction, piercing amber eyes shooting daggers straight through his skull. Phainon felt a chill creep down his spine, like the icy hand of death come to claim him. That should have been his first warning. It was the only one he would get.

One moment, Phainon was standing as the hairs on the back of his neck began to raise, and the next, he was flipped on his back with the pole of a spear pressing down on his neck. The prince tackled him to the marble, straddling his waist while something akin to a growl rumbled up from his throat.

“Now, you’re going to tell me exactly who you are, why you’re here, and how you got in, or this spear will paint the floor with your blood.”

Phainon let out a choked gurgle, pure ashwood bearing down on his throat and strangling the life out of him. Even if he wanted to satisfy the prince’s inquiry, he wouldn’t have been able to! Wasn’t this deeply counterintuitive to what he was trying to accomplish!?

“The appropriate response would be ‘Yes, your Grace’,” Mydeimos warned.

“Y-Y–agh!” Phainon rasped, grabbing onto the spear and shoving the prince backwards with it. “I don’t know– hACK-! How you expect me to answer you when you’ve got your spear against my windpipe!” Phainon hollered, practically scolded him. “Maybe you have a death wish, but I’d like to keep living a little longer, if you don’t mind, your Grace!”

Mydeimos stumbled between his legs, still pushing forward with the same amount of force it took Phainon to push back, leaving the spear motionless between them.

“Striking the prince outside of a duel is punishable by death, you know,” he grunted, an irritated quirk in his lip as his knuckles turned white with his vigor.

“You sure have a colorful way of showing your gratitude for the man who saved your life,” Phainon bit back, a sweat breaking out on his brow as he just barely kept the prince's furor at bay.

“Saved me? If you have your way, I'll be on a carriage bound for Ladon by sunrise tomorrow, on my way to lick a gross old pervert's unwashed ass for the rest of my days,” the prince fired back. “You've only delayed the inevitable.”

Their faces inched closer and closer as pure kinetic energy fired off all around them and charged the air with dynamite. Somehow, someway, the two were evenly matched in strength and willpower. Phainon never really got a good look at the prince's face until now, and even with his brows pulled together and a vein bulging from his forehead, he was just as handsome without his crown.

“...Is the King of Ladon really that ugly?” Phainon chanced.

Mydeimos’ face darkened, leaning in so close Phainon could feel the breath from his nose tickle his peach fuzz. “He is the most repulsive man I've ever laid eyes upon.”

Phainon grimaced at the thought. A man so hideous that his betrothed would rather cast himself from the highest of cliffs as opposed to marrying him truly could only come from Ladon. Phainon laid one arm across the pole while the other propped up his cheek, lounging across the spear while the prince held it up.

“You know, that's actually been bothering me this whole time. Why would King Eurypon marry off his firstborn son and heir to a foreigner?” he pondered aloud.

Mydeimos seemed confused, his brows curled upward with a harshly judgemental sneer. “I… I'm not his firstborn son?”

…What? “Why does it sound like you're asking me?”

“Is it not common knowledge wherever you are from that King Eurypon's firstborn was a daughter?” Phainon's deathly silence while the circuits in his brain shorted prompted the prince's explanation, “I began transitioning when I was sixteen, well after the birth of my brother, who was named Eurypon's firstborn son. I am his firstborn child, but officially speaking, I am his secondborn son.”

Somewhere off in the distance, a glass shattered.

Phainon's gaze immediately dropped to his chest. They were big… but not that big!

“What! How!?” Phainon gawked. “I-I couldn't even tell! I mean… good for you. Jeez.”

Mydeimos seemed to puff up with pride while Phainon continued staring directly into his sternum. The chest was the window to the soul, or however that old saying went.

“Thank you.”

“But still, that doesn't explain why you're being married off like it's nothing. Wouldn't that screw up the whole line of succession and– I'm sorry, I really have to know, actually, how?” Phainon repeated. Mydeimos’ physique would be impressive for anyone, let alone a son born a daughter.

“Gender affirming care,” Mydeimos astutely informed him. “My father made sure I had access to the best practitioners in all of Amphoreus.”

“Well,” Phainon breathed out, finally peeling his eyes from Mydeimos’ shapely chest to marvel at the sight of his perfectly sculpted jaw, as if Hephaestus himself had taken chisel to bone. “It does not show at all- I mean- in the best way possible. I seriously couldn't tell even for a second–” Phainon paused, really took a moment to digest, word for word, exactly what Mydeimos said. “...You said your dad? The one marrying you off to Ladon against your will?”

Mydeimos nodded. “Yes.”

“Wait, I'm sorry, hang on- he respects your gender identity but not your bodily autonomy?” Phainon clarified. “This guy's moral compass totally vexes me.”

Mydeimos sighed and dropped the spear, forcing Phainon to straighten out while he folded his hands in his lap. “Though they are historically our enemy, Ladon is strategically beneficial to his upcoming campaign against Okhema. He wanted their army, and their King wanted me. In his eyes, it was an easy decision,” Mydeimos explained while lifting himself off the ground. It was a good thing, too. Phainon isn't sure how much longer he would've survived with the prince practically tangled up in his legs.

“Define ‘upcoming campaign against Okhema’?” Phainon inquired, following the prince like a baby duckling while he returned to his room, leaning his spear against the wall before sitting at his vanity to start taking off his jewelry. “Okhema and Kremnos haven't warred with each other in half a century, no?”

“Correct. He plans on changing that,” Mydeimos said, unclasping his earring, lifting his heavy necklace over his head and laying it out around the pillow where his crown once was. Phainon wasn't sure when would be an appropriate time to give that back. “You can warn the Okhemans, if you desire. Or don't. It won't matter to me. Kremnos will have a dead prince before the King of Ladon has a willing groom.”

Phainon dragged his hands across his face. Life certainly came at him fast. He was nothing more than a thief and commoner when he woke up that morning, and now he was embroiled in a full blown political conspiracy. This was too much to process at once; The prince's death wish, the king's questionable morals, the unwashed ass sitting the throne in Ladon who bartered for the prince like meat scraps and a conflict simmering which was soon to explode. If Kremnos and Okhema were to come to blows, the whole of Amphoreus would feel it.

Could nothing put a stop to it besides the prince's death? Would his passing have the unintended consequence of severing Ladon's agreement with Kremnos? Would the duplicitous King withdraw his support if he could not have his living, breathing prize?

The way Phainon saw it, granted he had no training of any kind in sensitive diplomatic affairs, geopolitics or mental health counseling, there was a much, much simpler option staring him in the face.

“A word of advice?” Phainon tested.

“Go right ahead,” Mydei shrugged, removing his heavy gauntlets and the belt about his waist while his robe partially slipped down his shoulder.

With a deep breath in, Phainon clasped his hands together and took a leap of faith. “Have you considered just killing your dad?”

Phainon could see Mydeimos’ eyes perk up from the mirror he sat before. There was a spark of wonder glittering in his pupils, which seemed to narrow almost like a cat's while he mulled over the thought. “What did you say your name was?” He turned over his shoulder to meet Phainon's gaze.

Phainon stood stiff as a board, looking in both directions before settling on the prince's reflection rather than his eyes. “I didn't, actually… It's Phainon.”

“Phainon,” Mydeimos repeated, rolling off his tongue smooth like butter. “Where are you from, Phainon?”

“A-Aedes Elysiae,” Phainon tentatively responded.

“Never heard of it. Where is that?”

“I think I'd prefer it if you didn't know.”

Mydeimos stirred on this for a moment before shrugging his shoulders. “Fair enough. Does Aedes Elysiae teach you the two paths to ascending the throne in Kremnos?”

Phainon slowly nodded. It was one of those paths that got him into the palace so easily and inconspicuously, after all. The simplest transfer of power was by birth, typically a monarch's firstborn child, son or daughter. The next was still straightforward, but by no means simple; For anyone else who hoped to one day sit the ruby throne, they must first defeat the King and any birthright heirs who wished to defend their claim in ritualistic combat.

“And do they teach you about the tenacity of the Kremnoan spirit? And how highly we value our honor?”

Phainon gulped and nodded again, feeling like a gazelle in an open veldt.

“Good. Then you know the only way I could kill my own kin with my honor still intact would be to defeat him in a duel. And, as the King, defeating him in combat would mean that I would become the King of Kremnos by law.”

Phainon was really struggling to see the problem here. “Yes? Aren't you already the crown prince? You were next in line for the throne anyways-”

Mydeimos’ fist slammed his vanity, prompting Phainon to flinch and balk away. “Why do you assume I want the throne? My own family mourns my place in the line of succession more than the fact that I will be nothing more than a glorified bedslave to a foreign King who only wanted me because I am a man with a flowered cunt. Nobody has even thought to ask me what I want, because it is not my duty to want. It is my duty to be a son and a warrior and a leader, and when my father has more use for me as a pawn than any of those, then I'm expected to want nothing more!”

Mydeimos’ tantrum left him breathless, bare chest heaving beneath the weight of his tempered rage. Phainon did feel bad for him, truly. He didn't know much of the former crown prince, but those tapestries on the walls painted an accurate picture to the tales they told of him. He was a born lion, fierce and unwavering and free, and now he was going to be caged, muzzled and sent off to the circus. If Phainon were in his position, he'd go stir-crazy.

“What do you want, Prince Mydeimos?” Phainon asked.

Mydeimos’ vitriol wavered, features softening, back muscles loosening, shoulders dropping. He looked sad, in a way.

“I just want to keep being Mydei. The warrior-prince of Kremnos. And I want to have an orgasm before I die. It doesn't seem as though Lachesis has woven either of these things for me.”
